case_name: Milton H. Thomas II and Priscilla Snelling Thomas v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Two daughters, ET and EMT, both in postsecondary education in 2015.

adjustments: disallowed nonrefundable education credit of $3,000 and refundable American Opportunity Credit of $2,000 for failure to supply supporting information
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: American Opportunity Credit for daughter ET
conceded: Respondent conceded petitioners substantiated $2,885 of education expenses for 2015
Respondent conceded petitioners are entitled to the American Opportunity Credit for younger daughter EMT

findings_of_fact.fact: ET enrolled at Columbus State University from fall 2011 through fall 2015; nine semesters plus summer school (4 1/2 years); bachelor's degree December 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: ET, was enrolled at Columbus State University in Columbus, Georgia, from fall 2011 through fall 2015.

findings_of_fact.fact: On Form 8863 for 2015 petitioners claimed nonrefundable education credit of $3,000 and refundable AOC of $2,000 for ET and EMT
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioners claimed the nonrefundable education credit of $3,000 and the refundable American Opportunity Credit of $2,000.

findings_of_fact.fact: AOC claimed for ET for 2011 (also for petitioner wife), and solely for ET for 2012-2014; five taxable years total for ET (2011-2015)
findings_of_fact.snippet: In total petitioners claimed the American Opportunity Credit in relation to ET's postsecondary education for five taxable years (2011 through 2015).

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioners had claimed and received the AOC for ET for four taxable years 2011 through 2014
findings_of_fact.snippet: The record shows that by 2015 petitioners had claimed and received the American Opportunity Credit for four taxable years (2011 through 2014)

issues.question: Are petitioners entitled to the American Opportunity Credit for 2015 with respect to daughter ET, for whom the credit was claimed for 2011-2014?
issues.holding: No; the credit is allowed for only four taxable years per eligible student and was already claimed for ET for 2011-2014
issues.computable_reason: Four-prior-taxable-years limit of §25A(i)(2)/(b)(2)(A) applied to count of prior elections

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: AOC for ET disallowed for 2015 (four-year limit); AOC for EMT and $2,885 expenses allowed by concession

notes: Amounts rounded to nearest dollar. Notice of deficiency dated October 2, 2017. Facts partly stipulated.
